branch.commitSubject: fix(qc): neutralize repo-relative config paths in the camp01 live probe's synthetic config
branch.author: Wes Rollings <wrollings@gmail.com>

edits: failingPlaywrightConfig: added `globalSetup: undefined,` and `globalTeardown: undefined,` to the generated config literal.
failingPlaywrightConfig: added the `export` keyword so the guard asserts against the real generator rather than a transcription.
Added a 9-line why-comment above the function stating the scratch-directory resolution rule, why the hooks are DROPPED rather than absolutized, and where the guard lives.

files.shape: Declaration-held-against-reality guard, same pattern as src/__tests__/unit/e2eHarness/warmupDeclaration.test.ts (the guard #1544 itself added for warm-up routes).
files.mechanism: Reads playwright.config.ts as TEXT (importing it pulls @playwright/test into Jest and crashes before a row runs), extracts every top-level key whose value is a relative path literal via /^ {2}([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*): (['"])(\.\.?\/[^'"]*)\2\s*,/gm, reaches failingPlaywrightConfig through a spawned ESM harness (the convention the rest of the camp01 script suite uses), and requires every declared key to be neutralized (undefined/null) or absolutized.

shortstat.vsTarget: Target was ~80-105 lines across 2 files. Files landed on target (2); line count overshot by ~1.9x. The overshoot is comment density, not extra behavior: the guard carries a 33-line header explaining the outage, a docblock on each of its 4 helper functions, and a why-comment on each of its 4 rows, matching the precedent file (warmupDeclaration.test.ts, 195 lines) and the CLAUDE.md 'every function needs a comment' rule. Executable surface is ~60 lines; the .mjs edit is 14 insertions / 1 deletion.

redFirst.order: Guard authored and run BEFORE the neutralizer was added. The `export` keyword landed with the guard so the red would be about the unneutralized key, not a missing export.
failingRows: neutralizes or absolutizes every relative-path key the config declares
drops the server-dependent lifecycle hooks rather than re-pointing them
goes red when the base config gains an unneutralized relative-path key
redFirst.decisiveAssertion: unneutralizedRelativePathKeys(realConfig, generated) returned ['globalSetup'] -- the guard named the exact key the 13-day outage turned on, from the real config rather than a fixture.
redFirst.passingRow: finds relative-path keys to hold the override list against (the anti-vacuity row: the parser did match, so the other reds are real findings, not parse failure).

green.postCommitRerun: Re-run against the committed tree after the pre-commit hook's lint-staged pass: 4 passed, 4 total (guards against the known oxfmt quote-flip reformatting the committed content out from under the green).

gates.note: The 10 skips are the suite's pre-existing skips, unchanged by this commit. browserFreeConfigLoadProof.purpose: Execute the probe's config-load step -- the step that has been dying since 2026-09-02 -- without launching a browser. `playwright test --list` performs config load plus test collection and starts nothing; webServer is undefined and globalSetup is now dropped, so no server and no warm-up run.
browserFreeConfigLoadProof.harness: A scratchpad ESM script imported the SHIPPED failingPlaywrightConfig, wrote it plus the probe-shaped spec (absolute @playwright/test resolution, as deliberatelyFailingSpec does) into an mkdtemp root outside the repo, and ran `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test --config=<scratch>/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium --list` with cwd=repoRoot -- the probe's own cwd/config split.

rejectedAlternativesHeld: Did NOT re-home the synthetic config into the repo root (breaks the probe's out-of-repo isolation intent).
Did NOT absolutize globalSetup (it would then RUN, issuing HTTP warm-up against a server the synthetic config never starts -- webServer is undefined by design).
Did NOT revert #1544 (it is a real fix for finding #60; the defect is the probe's override list, not the config).
